analysis:
Examined CI threat-review scanner test files only; no provider, coordinator, or native-runtime code is changed, so no threat-model asset (A-001..A-017), boundary (TB-002..TB-011), or threat (T-041, T-053, etc.) is affected.

.github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py head 949-982 adds three tests:
- A manual GitHub rerun (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2) must hand off with MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED, make no paid calls, and never return clean.
- Scanner runtime is bounded to 60-3000s and defaults to 900s.
- A Bedrock workload ceiling stops at the unadmitted integration stage without clearance.

These tests assert fail-closed behavior: no clearance, no spend, and diagnostics without private content. .github/scripts/test-threat-diagnostics.py head 186-187,196 asserts that integrate() plans calls per reduction tier ([2,1]) via paid.plan_calls.

The tests use synthetic tokens only and expose no secrets. The remaining test lines are unchanged context. The scanner implementation (budget_scan, bedrock, threat-model-review.py runtime_seconds) is not supplied, so whether production code enforces these contracts is unverified. That is a coverage limit, not a security regression in this PR's evidence.
